estimates.measure_detail: Textual embedding analysis of similarity among the creative products. The embedding model, exact similarity metric, comparison pool, aggregation, and statistical model are not stated. The main text reports only that similarity did not significantly increase with AI.

sources.locator: PDF p. 21, Experiment 1, Supplementary Analysis, second analysis
sources.quote: we employed textual analysis techniques (embedding) to assess the similarity of the creative products.

sources.locator: PDF p. 21, Experiment 1, Supplementary Analysis, second analysis
sources.quote: Interestingly, our findings showed no significant increase in similarity among AI-assisted outputs compared to those created independently, indicating that AI use in our study did not homogenize creative work.

estimates.notes: Retained as a qualitative AI-versus-no-AI contrast, not described as a subgroup analysis. It is not a zero effect. The PDF prints no arm levels, numerical effect, standard error, test statistic, confidence interval, exact p-value, or similarity-analysis count (PDF p. 21). The study-level participation count is not substituted for an unstated analysis-specific count. Counts n_treatment, n_control, n_total, and n_units remain null. The task assigns a flash-fiction output to each person (PDF p. 16); similarity among these outputs supports question across_people and construct diversity. The embedding metric, comparison pool, aggregation, and observation unit are not specified, so unit remains null. Higher similarity means more_similar. GPT-4 was available while the treatment stories were written, so outcome_with_ai is true and timing is immediate. People were assigned to one of two conditions, with no crossover, so within_person is null (PDF pp. 15-17; Figure 1, PDF p. 48). No numerical uncertainty is reported, so se_basis is not_reported. The supplementary similarity model is not specified: the post-treatment adjustment documented for the separate creativity regressions is not assumed here. Online Appendix D is cited for further supplementary details on PDF p. 22 but was unavailable. Empty sources.fields lists accompany qualitative evidence; no numerical estimate was inferred.

estimates.notes: The authors describe increased similarity among AI-assisted outputs compared with outputs created without AI and explicitly repeat the Experiment 1 embedding analysis (PDF pp. 28-29; compare PDF p. 21). This supports an experiment-level across_people/diversity contrast under extraction-spec rule 4. The passage does not restrict this result to a human-capital subgroup or describe within-person idea variety. This corrects the earlier S2-O7 exclusion in the extraction and differs from the screening form, which withheld the classification pending the exact comparison pool. The exact pool of compared outputs, aggregation, embedding model, observation unit, and handling of multiple submissions by some participants remain unspecified (PDF pp. 24, 28-29). The study-level participant and work totals are not substituted for the unreported similarity-analysis counts; n_treatment, n_control, n_total, and n_units are null. Both arm levels, SDs, numerical SEs, intervals, and a test statistic are unreported. A coefficient and exact p-value are printed, but the uncertainty unit is unknown, so se_basis is unclear. The similarity regression specification, covariates, and outcome standardization are not reported; regression.outcome_scale is null. The post-treatment rater AI-identification adjustment documented for the separate creativity-rating regressions is not assumed for this unspecified similarity model. Participants were assigned to AI assistance or no AI, with AI available during the week-long lyric-production task (PDF p. 23); outcome_timing is immediate, outcome_with_ai is true, and within_person is null. Online Appendices A-F are absent from the saved manuscript; the linked OSF API and project-page requests failed with WinError 10013 during the fix review. No quantities were calculated from the p-value or imputed from another analysis.

open_items: Obtain unadjusted AI-versus-no-AI contrasts or models omitting post-treatment covariates for all human-rated creativity outcomes. The main-text regression tables all include rater AI identification. Arm-specific means, participant-level SDs, and arm analysis counts are not printed; full-sample descriptives cannot substitute for them (PDF pp. 19, 26, 40-47).

Exact randomized totals, arm sizes, and attrition by arm remain unreported. Experiment 1 gives a participation/final sample count, not a separately labeled randomized count (PDF p. 16). Experiment 2 distinguishes registration/IQ-test, information, submission, and selected analysis stages (PDF pp. 23-24). The subgroup sizes in AI-interaction analyses do not explicitly identify full-arm totals and were not added to create counts (PDF pp. 21, 28).

For S1-O4, obtain both arm levels, the embedding model and metric, the compared-output pool, aggregation and analysis units, the analysis-specific person count, model covariates, and numerical uncertainty. The saved PDF reports only a qualitative significance conclusion (PDF p. 21).

For S2-O7, obtain the exact compared-output pool, aggregation and observation unit, embedding model, handling of multiple submissions from one participant, model specification and covariates, outcome scaling, analysis-specific counts, both arm levels, SDs/SEs, and intervals (PDF pp. 24, 28-29). The cosine-similarity and L2-distance coefficients and exact p-values are now retained as across_people/diversity contrasts on the basis of the authors' explicit AI-versus-no-AI output-homogenization comparison; the exact comparison pool and participant dependence remain unresolved. Do not substitute study totals for unreported similarity-analysis counts or assume participant-level uncertainty.

Participant dependence in Experiment 2 needs resolution: the regressions use works as observations and report robust SEs, with no stated clustering by participant. Some people supplied multiple works (PDF p. 24; Tables 4-8, PDF pp. 43-47).

Online Appendices A-F and posted analysis output remain unavailable. During reconciliation on 2026-10-10, Python urllib requests with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 and no personal identifier to https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/ynhtu/files/osfstorage/?view_only=31642f7caac74082940eb1153d4e9e55, then https://osf.io/ynhtu/?view_only=31642f7caac74082940eb1153d4e9e55, and https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/g49yd/ all failed with WinError 10013 (socket access forbidden). No supplement or protocol contents were inferred from these failures.

Confirm whether the related preregistration at https://osf.io/g49yd/ applies to the realized experiments and identifies a primary outcome. The local forms/data/c366.json audit describes planned AI-tool, AI-collaborator, and no-AI conditions, whereas this PDF reports AI and no-AI conditions. The manuscript makes no preregistration statement and the protocol could not be independently accessed in this session.
Experiment 2 recruitment country is not explicitly stated (PDF pp. 22-24). Chinese currency and the manuscript discussion do not establish all recruitment locations.
Cross-experiment participant overlap and overlap with other papers remain unstated. PDF p. 16, footnote 1 identifies a broader research project but no particular shared-sample paper.
The paper names GPT-4 but does not print a model release year or API snapshot; ai_tool.year is null (PDF p. 16).
